title: Occlusion-Aware Text-To-Image Generation
claim: Baseline generators lose count accuracy as scene density grows; ours keeps counts exact or near-exact while staying photorealistic.
layout: 2 rows by 4 columns, baseline over ours, density increasing left-to-right
description: A grid of generated photographs with 4 columns of increasing density, labeled Low (N=3), Medium (N=6), High (N=12) and Very High (N=25). Each column has a quoted prompt above it, with object counts in red, yellow and blue. The top row is labeled Baseline and the bottom row is labeled Ours. The columns show swans in a pond, green apples in a basket, a restaurant table with bottles, plates and wine glasses, and a crowded kitchen with people and cans. Each image has a rounded count badge in its top-right corner: 3/3, 7/6, 7/12 and 50+/28 for baseline, and 3/3, 6/6, 12/12 and 24/28 for ours. Badges are green for correct, orange or red for failures, and yellow for near-correct. Small colored numerals overlaid on the objects mark individual instances. The eye goes first to the count badges, then to the contrast between the rows.
caption: Count-preserving multi-category compositional generation. Standard diffusion models (top) succeed on simple prompts (3/3 swans) but fail as scene complexity grows - overcounting single-category scenes (7/6 apples), dropping instances in multi-category compositions (7/12 across bottles, plates, and glasses), and catastrophically merging objects in dense scenes (50+/28 across persons and cans). Our approach (bottom) achieves exact or near-exact counts across all density levels (3/3, 6/6, 12/12, 24/28) while preserving photorealistic quality and natural inter-object occlusion.
abstract: Text-to-image diffusion models fail to generate correct object counts in dense scenes, where overlapping instances collapse into indistinguishable structures despite appearing visually plausible. We identify this as instance ownership collapse: tokens from overlapping objects interact freely through attention, while heavily occluded instances receive weak supervision due to their small visible areas. We address this through layout-aware attention biases that softly bias token interactions toward region-consistent grouping and suppress cross-instance leakage, paired with an amodal-balanced loss that amplifies gradients for occluded objects based on their occlusion level. To enable systematic evaluation, we introduce OverlapDepth-45K, a benchmark of densely overlapping scenes with amodal supervision. Our approach substantially improves count accuracy and prevents instance merging while preserving image quality.
